goal: Get through Mrs. Thornbury's card party without embarrassing her mother or her sister
conflict: Mrs. Thornbury has told the neighbourhood the Pellows have six thousand pounds, and Mr. Haverstock's attentions to Louisa seem to rest on it
crisis: Tell Mr. Haverstock the truth and expose the family's poverty to the room, or let the report stand and let Louisa be courted on a false footing
decision: Tells Mr. Haverstock quietly, at the tea table, that the family has barely five hundred pounds
key_actions: Sophia plays a dull rubber of whist with Mrs. Thornbury;Mrs. Thornbury boasts of the Pellows' fortune across the card table, and Mrs. Pellow does not contradict her;Mr. Haverstock asks Sophia whether her sister's fortune is settled on her;Sophia tells him the truth at the tea table;Mr. Haverstock thanks her coolly and returns to the card tables;Sophia sees Louisa has watched them speak
key_dialogue: Mrs. Thornbury: "Six thousand, my dear, and every penny of it in the funds";Sophia to Haverstock: "My sister has a great many perfections, sir, but a fortune is not among them"
motifs: cards and chance;money spoken of in company
subtext: Sophia loves her sister too well to let her be married for a sum she does not have, and suspects she is also a little jealous
